payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_a_cell_the_runtime_cannot_exec_in_exports_its_patch_from_the_volume stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cell/session.py. The claim was 'When `session.export_patch`\'s patch read from the cell fails, it first removes the cell\'s container with `runtime.remove_container`. The worktree volume is kept. Once that removal succeeds, it drops the container\'s name from the `created` set it is handed. Then it reads all four again from the worktree volume: the commit subjects, the patch, the head sha and the changed files. Each read goes through `runtime.run_ephemeral`, in a fresh container of the image the export is handed. That container gets no `env` and exactly one mount, the volume handed, read-only at `worktree.WORKTREE_MOUNT`. Its network is `saffron-export-<spec id lowercased>`, which this export creates through `runtime.create_network`. That name is neither `saffron-cells-<id>` nor `saffron-critic-net-<id>`. A network of that name is removed before the create and again after the last read. `patch.diff` and `patch.json` then hold the same bytes a live cell\'s export writes, and the returned head sha and subjects are equal. When the volume\'s subject read fails and the cell read its subjects, the cell\'s subjects are returned. The one `exported` teardown line keeps the base text `exported N bytes to <path>`, then names the volume and the cell\'s patch read error. The cell\'s own "commit subjects are unreadable" line is not emitted on this path. A cell whose patch read succeeds keeps its container, and the container\'s name stays in `created`. It starts no such container and creates no network, and its `exported` line is the base text exactly. When only its subject read failed, it emits the base\'s `commit_subjects` line, returns no subjects and writes its patch as at base. The witness drives a live cell, the same volume behind a dead cell whose subject and patch reads both fail, and a live cell whose subject read alone fails. Each reads a rename under a global git config that sets `diff.noprefix`.', and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
